acceptanceCriteria.statement: On the home screen, a left-aligned headline stack and a single primary call to action are visible above the fold on desktop.
The same top navigation item order appears on home and pricing.
At the mobile breakpoint, pricing tiers collapse into a single vertical column while preserving tier order.
At the mobile breakpoint, the home hero collapses into a single vertical stack.
Keyboard focus remains visibly indicated on interactive elements in navigation and hero areas.
Neither inspected screen introduces a second primary call to action or a competing conversion path.

accessibilityAndRecovery: If a keyboard user tabs into the page, the focus outline must remain clearly visible on nav links and hero actions.
If mobile stacking causes long labels to wrap, the layout must allow vertical growth instead of truncation that hides meaning.
If a comparison element fails to load decorative imagery, the pricing hierarchy must still read correctly from text order and headings alone.
assumptions: The exact typography is not specified in the brief, so type treatment will be original and chosen to support the preserved hierarchy rather than to match the source.
The specific pricing labels are not provided in the evidence, so the adaptation will use original tier names and content while preserving the tier structure.
The exact visual styling of buttons, cards, and navigation is not grounded in the evidence, so those components will be redrawn with original branding.
Any route or content not present in the inspected home and pricing pages is assumed unavailable for design decisions unless separately inspected.

principles: Retain the repeated top navigation pattern so home and pricing read as one site.
Keep the hero’s left-aligned headline stack paired with a single primary call to action above the fold on home.
Use the inspected mobile collapse behavior as the responsive rule: multi-column regions reduce to one column and pricing tiers remain vertically ordered.
Preserve visible keyboard focus styling for interactive elements.
Avoid copying any source-specific wordmark, palette, copy, illustrations, or iconography; substitute original equivalents instead.
globalDirection.summary: Create an original B2B marketing surface that preserves the inspected site’s information structure while replacing source-specific branding with new content and neutral visual treatment.

accessibility: Interactive elements must show a visible keyboard focus indicator.
Navigation order must be preserved so the first actions remain discoverable from keyboard and pointer input.
failureAndRecovery: If the hero content overflows at small widths, the layout must stack before clipping occurs.
If the primary action is not visible in the initial viewport, it must remain reachable by scrolling without requiring horizontal scrolling.
mobileRules: hero columns collapse to a single vertical stack at the mobile breakpoint
primary call to action remains reachable without horizontal scroll
screenBlueprints.summary: Home should establish the value proposition immediately with a left-aligned headline stack, one primary action, and the shared top navigation repeated from pricing.

accessibility: Interactive elements must show a visible keyboard focus indicator.
Tier headings and actions must remain in a logical reading order after stacking.
failureAndRecovery: If tier cards collide at narrow widths, they must reflow to a single column rather than overlap.
If a comparison action becomes ambiguous, the hierarchy should rely on order and heading structure rather than visual ornament.
mobileRules: pricing tiers stack vertically and preserve their tier hierarchy at the mobile breakpoint
screenBlueprints.summary: Pricing should present tier comparison beneath the same top navigation, with the tier hierarchy maintained when the layout compresses.

sourceDecisions.rationale: The same top navigation bar appears on both inspected routes, so keeping one shared nav preserves cross-page continuity without copying any branded content.
The home page hero is documented as a left-aligned headline stack above a single primary CTA; keeping that relationship supports immediate comprehension while avoiding multi-action clutter.
The inspected responsive behavior collapses multi-column hero content into one column on mobile; preserving that rule prevents horizontal overflow and keeps the hierarchy intact.
Visible keyboard focus is explicitly observed on interactive elements in hero and nav, so the migrated surface should keep a comparable focus treatment.
Source-specific wordmark, exact palette, and unique illustration language are not allowed by the brief and would make the migration derivative rather than original.
The authenticated account route was blocked and not inspected, so no interaction or content decision may depend on that screen.
